widgets_values:
Color-range segmentation playground (chroma key)

BGR -> HSV so 'green+cyan' is one hue interval instead of a diagonal slab of RGB space, then cv2_inRange picks every pixel between the two 'CV Scalar' bounds (H, S, V) - type other bounds to key a different color (OpenCV hue is 0..179: green ~35-85, blue ~90-130, red wraps around 0). Morphological open/close cleans speckles and pinholes. The mask then cuts the subject out and composites it over a second image, resized to match via 'CV Array Size' feeding cv2_resize's dsize. A photo with no keyed color at all simply yields an empty mask and the untouched original - nothing fails.

nodes.title: [CV Color Range] Color Range: pink across the 179/0 seam
Pink mask (inRange can't wrap in one pass)
[CV Color Range From Sample] Color Range From Sample: measure pink's band
Preview as Text: Learned tolerance (sigma * spread)

widgets_values: Two higher-level colour-range nodes that complement the raw inRange above. 'CV Color Range' keeps pixels within a tolerance of a CENTER colour and is hue-aware: with format 'hue in channel 0, period 180' a band centred on RED hue across the 179/0 seam in ONE pass (raw inRange would need two ranges + an OR). 'CV Color Range From Sample' then samples the pixels inside a region (here the red mask we just made; normally a scribble or an 'Annotate Points' polygon) and MEASURES the band - its circular mean puts the learned hue centre back near 164/180, and it outputs that centre and the sigma*spread tolerance to inspect or feed back into 'CV Color Range'.

BackProject (bg histogram, invert): crop a background strip (0,0,60x497), convert with HSV_FULL, CalcHist on S+V channels (16x16 bins, 'peak' norm), CalcBackProject on full image, THRESH_BINARY_INV at 1, then refined via morphologic operations. MedianBlur(9) pre-filters noise; a larger BG crop + inverted threshold separates foreground from uniform background. 
Note: HSV_FULL gives uniform 0-256 ranges across all 3 channels (H range doubles to 256 vs standard 180). The two subgraph morph nodes ('cv2.morphology (simple)') accept proxyWidgets for op/ksize_x/ksize_y.
